text:
Priya: @Sam FYI — multiple customers hit intermittent CI deploy failures since ~2024-06-28 22:00 UTC. Errors show 403 when CI runner tries to impersonate the service account. Collecting logs below, but impact: ~15% of nightly jobs failing, some deploys blocked.

deploy-bot: automated alert — 5 failures in the last 30m for project/redwood/edge-runner (#752, #753, #755, #759, #762) :warning:

Priya: paste of one failing job log:
```
[2024-06-28T22:14:05Z] ci-runner: requesting token for impersonation: ci-deploy-sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com
[2024-06-28T22:14:06Z] STS: success, got token (exp=1719954446)
[2024-06-28T22:14:06Z] API call: POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/deploys -> 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "Permission denied",
  "message": "Caller does not have permission to perform iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on serviceAccount: projects/123/serviceAccounts/ci-deploy-sa@...",
  "code": 403
}
```

Sam: can you repro locally? two quick things: 1) paste the raw id token header/payload (just exp/aud/permissions claim if any), 2) does `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=...` return a token with the expected scopes/claims?

Priya: repro steps I used (from affected customer):
1) `gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=https://internal-api.redwood.local --impersonate-service-account=ci-deploy-sa@...`
2) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/deploys` -> 403 (see log).

Priya: token payload (redacted):
```
{
  "iss": "https://sts.googleapis.com/",
  "sub": "system:serviceaccount:ci-runner:ci-runner",
  "aud": "https://internal-api.redwood.local",
  "exp": 1719954446,
  "iat": 1719954146
}
```

Jordan: we shipped an IAM policy tightening last night on the CI role to enforce least-privilege: removed `iam.serviceAccounts.get` from the ci-runner role and replaced with a narrow `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` binding conditioned on `requestor.project == deployed_project` for instances launched after 2024-06-28T21:30Z. Could be a propagation/condition edge-case.

Alec: I rolled that change — intended. We added a time-bound IAM condition to avoid service accounts being used across teams. We did test but not at this scale. Quick guess: some runners still have cached credentials minted before the change that don't match the new condition and are getting rejected, or our token broker is issuing tokens with stale audience/scope.

Sam: hmm — two failure modes I can think of: 1) Token TTL too short and token broker reuses/refreshes incorrectly under race, producing tokens that lack the new condition attributes, 2) Policy condition uses `request.time` or `request.auth.claims` and STS token doesn't include the attribute the condition checks.

Priya: customer reported it happens mid-pipeline — first job step works, later step (after a docker pull) fails. Suggests token rotation in the pipeline and a short-lived token race.

ci-runner-bot: CI runner debug snapshot for attempt #759:
```
ENV: runner-vm-22, image: redwood/ci:v2.1
IMPERSONATE: ci-deploy-sa@...
TOKEN_TTL: 300s
TOKEN_MINT_TIME: 2024-06-28T22:14:06Z
TOKEN_EXP: 2024-06-28T22:19:06Z
API_CALL_TIME: 2024-06-28T22:14:07Z -> 403
```

Sam: actionable repro we can run in staging:
1) create a CI job that impersonates `ci-deploy-sa` and sets TOKEN_TTL=300
2) start job and artificially sleep the runner for 90s between steps to force a refresh during the pipeline
3) watch for 403s and capture the raw token and `gcloud iam policies test` traces.

Alec: temporary mitigation options:
- revert the IAM condition to allow the previous flow (fast but broad)
- increase token TTL on broker to 1h to avoid rotation races (short-term)
- add a fallback service account for old runners and gradual rollout (safer)

Jordan: long-term fix: make broker mint tokens that include the IAM condition attribute we rely on (e.g., include `requestor_project` as claim) or switch to signed JWT assertions that satisfy condition. Also make the console/runner pull fresh policy and invalidate caches on IAM change.

Priya: customer-facing workaround I posted: set `CI_IMPERSONATE_FALLBACK=true` to use the dedicated deploy token (we can create one with limited lifetime) until we fix. Asked for customer acknowledgement.

Sam: I'll run the staging repro now and file an infra bug if I can reproduce. Can one of you (Alec/Jordan) revert the change or whitelist the flagged projects temporarily? If not, I'll script the TTL bump as a stop-gap.

Alec: I'll whitelist the top 3 affected projects for next 6 hours and open a rollback PR.

Priya: thanks. Action items: Sam — run repro + open bug (S-1238). Alec — whitelist and PR. Jordan — design token-broker claim patch. Priya — notify affected customers & add note to status page. :white_check_mark:

Sam: noted. I'll paste repro logs into the bug once done. :thumbsup:

Priya: closing the thread once PR deployed or we have a confirmed repro. Keeping this thread for updates.
